name: Multimodal Enterprise RAG
blurb: A local retrieval system built to explore knowledge spread across text, images, audio, and video. It brings together OCR and transcription with vector search, then makes related information explorable through a knowledge graph. The prototype uses Streamlit for the interface, Ollama for local model workflows, and Qdrant for vector storage, with Python connecting the pipeline.

name: Personal LLM Chatbot
blurb: A document question-answering project that lets a user ingest files and chat with a locally run language model through a Flask interface. Its focus is the bridge between document input, a web application, and Ollama-powered local inference. The repository adapts ideas from the credited Ollama and privateGPT projects.

name: Image Classifier
blurb: A computer-vision course project that applies transfer learning to classify flower images. The workflow includes saving trained checkpoints and running predictions from the command line, including a top-K list of likely classes. It is implemented in Python with PyTorch.

name: OS LLM Agent
blurb: An experiment in connecting a locally hosted Ollama model to operating-system-oriented tools. The repository explores an agent loop and MCP tool-server integration, with Python handling the experiments and tool connections. It is an exploration of the interaction pattern rather than a claim of a production-ready system.

name: OpenAI Desktop GUI
blurb: A small desktop application for entering prompts and viewing responses from the OpenAI API. Tkinter provides the window and input/output interface, while Python handles the request flow. The project explores a straightforward desktop front end for model interaction.

name: Transistor Fine-Tuning and Tool-Use Evaluation
blurb: Research evaluating vision-language models on transistor analysis and TCAD tool use. The study compares a base model with adapter fine-tuning, examines guided error analysis, and explores persistent memory as part of the workflow. Experiments use Python, PyTorch, VLMs, and TCAD; results and limitations are recorded separately so the evaluation is not presented as more conclusive than it is.

name: Qiskit ket_basis Visualization
blurb: A merged contribution to Qiskit that adds X, Y, and Z ket-basis choices to quantum-state LaTeX visualization. The change includes tests and a release note, and was merged on October 22, 2026. It uses Python and Qiskit's quantum-computing visualization code.

name: Qiskit Transpiler Optimization Investigation
blurb: An investigation into a circuit-cancellation issue in Qiskit's transpiler. After reproducing the behavior, the proposed change was compared across circuit families; benchmarking recorded both gate reductions and the runtime overhead. This remains an investigation and is not represented as a merged contribution.

name: Minecraft Redstone Qubit Simulator
blurb: A Minecraft Java world that models a classical one-qubit stabilizer workflow using redstone logic. The build demonstrates X, Z, Hadamard, and measurement operations and is available to download from the repository. Two-qubit entanglement is a planned extension, not part of the current build.

name: ATS Scanner / ResuMaster
blurb: A Chrome extension that extracts a job description from a page and passes it into a PartyRock resume-review workflow using saved resume text. JavaScript and browser-extension APIs connect the page-reading step with the review experience. The project focuses on reducing repeated copy-and-paste during application review.

name: Snake Programming Language
blurb: A small language implementation in Node.js. Its interpreter is organized around a lexer and recursive-descent parser, with support for variables, conditionals, loops, and list operations. The project explores how source text moves through parsing and execution in a custom language.

name: Canvas Todos
blurb: A local dashboard that brings school calendar feeds together with todos, announcements, and assignments added manually. Python and HTML provide the application structure, while calendar feeds supply schedule information. It is designed to work without requesting Canvas API tokens.

name: Claude CLI MCP Bridge
blurb: A Python stdio MCP server that wraps a locally installed Claude CLI. It explores session continuation, configurable timeouts, and explicit tool permissions so an MCP client can interact with the local command-line workflow. The project is local and does not claim to host a remote service.

name: Python Revision History
blurb: A prototype for tracking document revisions with immutable snapshots, metadata, text comparisons, and restore-as-new-version behavior. Python's difflib supports textual comparison, while the versioning layer keeps prior states available for review. The current in-memory storage is not thread-safe.

name: Google Alert Automation
blurb: A Python automation that extracts links from Google Alert emails for follow-up processing. Email parsing handles the message content and turns embedded links into more accessible input for a subsequent workflow. The listed scope is link extraction.

name: College Info Scraper
blurb: An educational Python web-scraping project that collects college links and admissions-related information from websites. It explores extracting useful school data into a more organized form, with scraping as the core technique.

name: WhatsApp Scraping and Messaging
blurb: An educational browser-automation experiment using Python and Selenium to explore group-information extraction and messaging workflows. It documents automation mechanics in the browser; it is not presented as an official WhatsApp integration.

name: PlaygroundAI Discord Bot
blurb: A Python Discord bot that connects chat commands with browser-driven AI image-generation workflows. Discord provides the interaction surface and Selenium automates the browser portion of the workflow. The project explores joining a chat interface to an existing image-generation experience.

name: One Pace Player
blurb: An Electron video player built around episodic viewing. It includes arc-based navigation, saved playback progress, and next-episode playback so users can resume and move through a series from one desktop application. JavaScript and Electron form the application stack.

name: Streaming Video Downloader
blurb: A set of Python utilities for collecting streaming media links and supporting offline download workflows. The project explores the link-collection and download steps as separate utilities rather than describing a hosted streaming service.

name: Minecraft Mod
blurb: A Java modding project exploring custom Minecraft items, blocks, crops, and ore generation. It provides a practical sandbox for learning how game content additions fit into the Minecraft modding workflow.

name: Better Minescript
blurb: A Minecraft scripting and navigation prototype that exposes world queries, movement, interactions, GUI controls, and rendering APIs through Python and Java components on Fabric. Long-route navigation and later source fixes are still unvalidated, so those behaviors are described as ongoing work rather than confirmed features.

name: Minecraft Movement Mods
blurb: A collection of separate Minecraft movement experiments covering player locking, lunge swaps, sword knockback, and triple swapping. Java is used for the mod work, with each behavior and its debugging notes tracked independently rather than bundled as one finished feature.

name: Tacos Website
blurb: A Flask restaurant website with home and menu pages supported by food imagery. Python and Flask provide the web application, while HTML and CSS shape the pages. The project explores presenting a small restaurant offering through a simple multi-page site.

name: Risk Management
blurb: A Flask web interface for managing projects and a risk register. The pages support project editing and the creation, editing, and deletion of risks, with Python handling application behavior and HTML forming the interface. The project focuses on the core CRUD workflow for project risk information.

name: Web Backend
blurb: A Python backend repository organized into routers, data models, migrations, and shared utilities. SQL is part of the data layer. The structure explores how application endpoints and supporting backend components can be separated into maintainable modules.

name: Portfolio Website
blurb: The Flask-backed source for this portfolio, using a shared project catalog to keep project information consistent across pages. A static HTML export is generated from the same data so the portfolio can also be served without the Flask application. It uses Python, Flask, HTML, and CSS.

name: Earlier Portfolio Website
blurb: An earlier personal portfolio kept in a separate GitHub Pages repository. The archived site was built with HTML and SCSS and is retained as a record of an earlier version of the portfolio.

name: Frontend Test Page
blurb: A small HTML page used to experiment with frontend structure and presentation. It is a minimal learning project focused on browser-rendered markup.

name: Learn Python
blurb: A learning repository of Python exercises covering syntax, classes, data structures, functions, exceptions, file input/output, and modules. It provides a progression through core language concepts and practical small examples.

name: AI Study Assistant - Model Layer
blurb: A Java team-project contribution focused on the model layer of an AI study assistant. It implements query-session state, immutable responses, Observer notifications, and isolation from stale results, with Swing and JUnit in the listed stack. Full integration with the team GUI is still pending.

name: Photo Album Manager
blurb: A Java coursework project centered on photo-album management and application design. It explores how an application can organize album-related behavior within a Java program.

name: Robot Clone / Imitation Learning
blurb: A planning-stage concept exploring personalized software behavior alongside physical imitation learning from wearable demonstration data. The idea has not been built into a robot; robotics and imitation learning describe the proposed direction.

name: Matmul-Optimized Accelerator
blurb: A computer-architecture concept study about accelerating matrix multiplication. It examines systolic arrays, tiling, memory bandwidth, and data movement as design considerations; RTL and FPGA implementation are proposed next steps, not completed deliverables.
